content:
I stopped by to complain about my least favorite part of the entire core one assembly.  Todd mostly spelled it out already but I'd also like to add the lack of a disconnect for the sensor cable and the maximal disassembly and lack of accessibiliy to clear filament jams/breaks.

Please, if you are forced to include these sorts of blind assemblies then at least include features to datum the parts and retain them during assembly.  A simple printed tab and hole would have gone a long way.

Frankly though, I'd prefer to see this entire filament sensor assembly to be re-engineered to install & service outside of the panel.

I’d like to repeat here—with a slight modification—the assembly tip I shared after my initial setup 8 months ago (it now took me 5–10 minutes on my own, without any outside help):

Use masking tape — as an alternative to just lean it on its side:

a) Place an object about 32 mm high (e.g., a book) to the right of the printer and set the metal sheet assembly on top of it, leaning it against the right side of the printer.
b) Slide/tilt the side filament sensor assembly close to its final (IMPORTANT: upright) position between the smooth rod and the inner wall. It must be upright because the part CAN NO LONGER be tilted once the sheet metal assembly is secured according to step c).
c) Secure the upper section of the sheet metal assembly to the CoreXY plate with 2–3 strips of masking tape. This temporary fixation leaves both hands free for the subsequent installation of the filament sensor and the right handle. The 32mm side support is then no longer needed.
d) Remove the rear mounting screw from the right handle, align the threaded hole and the through hole, and temporarily screw the parts together. This is still a bit fiddly, but much easier than with the screw assembled in right handle.
e) Now it’s easy to screw the right handle into place — with the pre-installed front screw and slightly swiveled out — since the front threaded and through holes are now aligned.
f) Unscrew the rear, temporarily installed screw, swivel the right handle into its final position, and secure it with the rear screw.

The amount of unengineering for assembly is shocking in this step.  The filament sensor can’t be preassembled to the handle to the side piece because the Bowden tube length doesn’t allow for it.  The handle can’t be preattached to the side piece because the side piece holes arent tapped.  The side piece can’t rest on the table because it is too short.  The handle prohibits seeing the screw hole, etc, etc.  One of these dependencies should be eliminated on the next model.

I put a bit of plumbers putty (Playdoh would also work) inside the screw head, so at least the screw would stay attached to the driver.

Based on what anden3 said, I hung the left side by two rivets. Then I used a flashlight, and lined up the filament sensor's holes, and put the back screw partway in without the handle. Put the front screw in the handle and put it through the front hole, then moved the filament sensor onto it. Got that most of the way in, then took out the back screw, rotated the handle into place, and ran the screw into the filament sensor.

Only needed two hands!

That filament sensor setup is a rough spot. If I have to take it apart to clear fractured filament, the panel gives me a hard time, so I'm finding easier ways to assemble it.

This step is just as hard as before... I recommend securing the left side with a longer bolt first, then securing the right side, and then replacing the left side. A second pair of hands to hold the panel is highly recommended.
